The tail gate of a marker with no density minimum, where it can be placed

Source: R/adaptive-thresholds.R
tail_gate_cut.Rd

Above the dominant mode, openCyto's default side, never below zero signal (a negative population ending below zero puts the cut at zero), and only where it leaves under 60% of the parent above it (more means the dominant mode was not a negative one). NOTHING above the cut is an answer rather than a failure: a viability dye in a sample with no dead cells, a marker no cell in this sample carries. Shared by the default path of resolve_threshold() and the last resort of best_threshold(), so the two cannot disagree on where a tail goes.

Usage

tail_gate_cut(x, floor = -Inf, side = c("upper", "lower"))

Arguments

x

transformed values within the parent gate.

floor

the transformed value of zero signal, -Inf for scatter.

side

"upper" (default), or "lower" where the analyst has declared the dominant mode positive; the cut is then the mode minus 3.5 SD and must leave over 40% of the parent above it.

Value

the cut, or NA where no tail gate can be placed.

Details

WHY THE SIDE IS NOT GUESSED. A single mode does not say whether it is the marker's negative or positive population. Its distance from zero signal does not either: granulocyte autofluorescence and the spillover spread of bright cells put a NEGATIVE mode well above zero, and a per-marker cofactor small enough to resolve the negatives stretches that offset into many standard deviations. A version that cut below any mode lying 3.5 of its SDs above zero took the lower side 17 times in two runs on one 24-sample whole-blood cohort scored against manual gating, and was wrong every time it could be checked: Vd1, Vd2 and CD11c, all rare, called positive on 90-99% of CD45+ cells, emptying CD4 and CD8 T cells (defined Vd1- Vd2-), and a CD16 cut below the bulk that took classical monocytes to 0% and non-classical to 12% (manual 6.4% and 0.1%). openCyto takes the side from the analyst for this reason. A marker carried by most of its parent with no density minimum gets a cut above its mode, flagged needs_review, unless the analyst declares the other side, as openCyto's side argument does: thresholds: <marker>: {tail: lower} in the configuration. A control, a fixed cut or a parent: in which the marker separates are the alternatives.
